body:
Myk's framing (2026-08-21), held here so the backlog carries it: the dream is deltas flowing
in every direction and state accumulating MEANINGFULLY; the nightmare is the same flows
producing delta soup — any store running long enough becomes a mess of noise nobody can stay on
top of. "We really need to hit that story hard." This is a follow-up to be designed IN PRECISE
DETAIL with Myk in a dedicated session — this stub exists so no session forgets it, and it is
NOT buildable as it stands. Do not pick it up for implementation; do not resolve its questions
by inference.

What the design session should weigh (gathered candidates, not decisions):
- The first anti-soup front is already ticketed as visibility: channel health (T203), contested
  names (T204), the grant ledger (T205), custody stamps (T207). Legibility precedes hygiene.
- Noise budgets at the write side: kyber's D5 rule (pulses are not facts; ephemeral events never
  become deltas) is the same instinct that made T207 attest only non-empty syncs. What is
  Loam's general form of that rule?
- Digest/attention surfaces at the read side: what changed since I last looked, per container,
  as a lens over ordinary deltas — the board's shape, generalized.
- Archival tiering: cold deltas that stop costing attention without stopping being true
  (relates to the archive mirror and §29's graveyard, but for the living store).
- The admin page as the anti-soup instrument: Myk names it the biggest gap today.

Acceptance criterion:
(a) A design session with Myk has produced a working spec (or a decision not to). Verify: the
    session's outcome replaces this stub — `adlc ticket update` narrows it into real tickets or
    archives it into the spec work it becomes.

Merge tier: not applicable — this ticket gates on a human design session by construction.
title: The delta-soup problem — the store that stays legible (DESIGN-STAGE STUB, awaiting Myk)
